# Network chapter source record
Original wording, diagrams, synthetic traces and worksheets drafted 14 October 2026. Standards are linked, not reproduced as teaching extracts. The Unit 3 editorial coverage map is available; independent review, conventions, learner evidence and certified alignment remain pending.
- Curriculum: SCSA 2026 Year 12 syllabus; models/transport and packet architecture. Official course page remains the authority.
- OSI: ITU-T X.200 (1994), https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.200-199407-I/en
- Internet layer convention: RFC 1122, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122.html
- TCP: RFC 9293, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html
- UDP: RFC 768, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768.html
- IPv4: RFC 791, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791.html
- ARP: RFC 826, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc826.html
- DNS supports TCP: RFC 7766, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7766.html
- HTTP/3: RFC 9114, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114.html
- Documentation addresses: RFC 5737, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5737.html
Ethernet arithmetic is explicitly limited to an untagged Ethernet II model: 14-byte header,4-byte FCS,46-byte minimum data field,1500-byte IP MTU; options and physical signalling/gap excluded.

- IPv4 Ethernet padding/MTU: RFC 894, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894.html
- Ethernet header/FCS fields: Cisco Troubleshooting Ethernet, https://www.cisco.com/en/US/docs/internetworking/troubleshooting/guide/tr1904.html
